episodes.title: Reading Blueprints
episodes.text: You arrive at the garage site. You open the blueprint on the hood of the van. You check where the wiring and charger box must go to meet code.

episodes.title: Setting Conduit
episodes.text: You measure the wall for the charger run. You cut conduit to length with a power tool. You set the conduit inside the marked partition.

episodes.title: Pulling Wire Again
episodes.text: You pull insulated wire through the conduit. You do the next run the same way. It is the same as yesterday. It will be the same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Up The Ladder
episodes.text: You climb the ladder to the high wall mount. You hold the charger fixture in place. The conduit below is ready and you start the install.

choice.prompt: The fixture holes do not line up with the conduit. Do you adjust now or keep going?

options.label: Climb down and remeasure
options.outcome: You climb down and remeasure with your tape. You mark the new spots and the fixture fits.

options.label: Force the fixture on
options.outcome: You try to force it from the ladder. The screws catch badly and you have to redo it anyway.

episodes.title: Charger Fault
episodes.text: You are on the ladder when the new charger stays dead.

choice.prompt: The charger has no power. What do you check first?

options.label: Test the circuit with your ammeter
options.outcome: You test the circuit and find no current. You trace the break back to a loose wire.

options.label: Keep assembling the parts
options.outcome: You keep working without testing. The charger stays dead and you still have to test.

chat.text: Any power at the box?
Check it with your test lamp before you touch more wire.

episodes.title: Testing The Circuit
episodes.text: You are back on the ground by the panel. You pick up your test lamp. You check the wiring you finished today.

trial.title: Run the conduit
items: Pull insulated wires through the conduit
Place conduit inside the designated wall partition
Connect the wires to complete circuits between boxes
Lay tubing along the marked path
trial.explain: You lay the run first, place it, pull wire, then connect.

episodes.title: Morning Client Call
episodes.text: You sit down with the customer at a small table. You ask what this meeting is for and who is coming. You write down their objectives and requirements.

choice.prompt: The customer wants a full conference program squeezed into one morning meeting. What do you ask next?

options.label: Ask which one objective matters most
options.outcome: You narrow the morning to the main objective. You note the other items for a later event.

options.label: Ask about budget and participant count
options.outcome: You get a headcount and a spending limit. You use them to sketch what the morning can actually hold.

options.label: Suggest cutting the attendee list
options.outcome: The customer pauses and keeps the full list. You keep all requirements and move on to timing.

episodes.title: Checking Vans and Rooms
episodes.text: You sit at your desk and check the same accommodation and transportation list as yesterday. You confirm room counts and pickup times again. Same sheet tomorrow.

episodes.title: Sorting Projectors and Displays
episodes.text: You stand in the storage room with your list. You check what audio-visual equipment and displays the event needs. You confirm transportation for the gear and arrange delivery to the site.

trial.title: Line up the gear
items: Confirm the displays and equipment are ready for the event
Note what audio-visual equipment and displays the event needs
Check availability of the equipment and transportation
Arrange delivery of the equipment, transportation, and displays
trial.explain: You list what is needed first, then check availability before you arrange anything.

episodes.title: Walkthrough With Site Staff
episodes.text: You meet the site staff in the main hall to go over the setup.

chat.text: Catering will use the side door, signage goes by the entrance.
Have you covered special needs access and printing?
Security wants the display layout before 3.

episodes.title: Bus Has Not Arrived
episodes.text: You get word the transportation for participants has not arrived at the site.

choice.prompt: Participants are waiting and the bus is missing. What do you do first?

options.label: Call the transportation provider and re-route
options.outcome: You reach dispatch and get a new pickup time. You tell participants when to expect the bus.

options.label: Arrange backup vans for special needs riders first
options.outcome: You secure accessible rides for those who need them. The rest of the group waits for the main bus update.

chat.text: Our group is waiting and no bus is here.
Catering is set, facilities are open.

episodes.title: Checking the Bills
episodes.text: You sit back at your desk with the event bills. You go through each charge line by line for accuracy. You approve payment for the correct ones.

episodes.title: Morning Calendar Review
episodes.text: You arrive and open the executives' calendars. You check today's meetings and move one overlap. You send the updated times to everyone.

episodes.title: Office Needs Pile Up
episodes.text: You sit with facilities and a personnel note to sort for the executive.

choice.prompt: Housekeeping and records both need attention now. What do you handle first?

options.label: Clear the records request first
options.outcome: You clear the records queue and housekeeping waits until later this morning.

options.label: Send housekeeping in first
options.outcome: You book housekeeping now and push the records work to the afternoon.

chat.text: Records room is full and housekeeping needs a time.
Can you set the order for us?

episodes.title: Payroll Line Check
episodes.text: You sit down with the payroll information. You check the same lines as yesterday. Same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Afternoon Invoices and Memos
episodes.text: You open your spreadsheet and word processing files. You draft an invoice and a short memo. You check the numbers and save both.

trial.title: Put the document in order
items: Save the finished file
Check the numbers for errors
Enter the figures in the spreadsheet
Open the invoice template
trial.explain: You open the template before you enter and check anything.

episodes.title: Travel Falls Through
episodes.text: You learn the executive's booked trip no longer works. You pull up the travel plan and the calendar. You need to fix it fast.

choice.prompt: The trip time clashes with a meeting you manage. What do you do?

options.label: Rebook the travel around the meeting
options.outcome: You make new travel arrangements and keep the schedule as it is.

options.label: Move the meeting to save the travel
options.outcome: You shift the schedule and keep the original travel booking.

options.label: Hold both and ask the executive
options.outcome: You pause changes and wait for a quick answer before you act.

episodes.title: Budget and Files Close
episodes.text: You gather departmental finances and budget notes. You file the records and update the totals. You leave the folder ready for the executive.

episodes.title: Listening To The Tractor
episodes.text: You arrive at the shop and walk out to the tractor with the farmer waiting beside it.

choice.prompt: You hear the knock and see the old report. What do you check first?

options.label: Run it uphill and listen close
options.outcome: You hear the knock clearly under load and narrow it to the engine. You note where to open it up.

options.label: Start with the inspection report
options.outcome: You read the past notes and match them to what you hear now. You mark the likely spot to test next.

chat.text: It knocks bad when I push it uphill.
The inspection sheet from last week is on the seat.

episodes.title: Taking It Apart
episodes.text: You roll the tractor into the bay and shut it down. You pick up your hand tools and start taking off the covers around the bad spot.

trial.title: Strip it down safe
items: Split the housing to reach the broken part
Lay the bolts and parts out in order
Shut the tractor down and make it safe
Pull the covers off with hand tools
trial.explain: You make it safe first, then open it step by step.

episodes.title: Overhauling The Harvester
episodes.text: You move to the harvester for its full service. You change worn parts, adjust belts, and check the irrigation pump beside it. You work through each system with your hands.

episodes.title: Same Bolts Again
episodes.text: You sit back down with the service checklist. You go through the same grease points and fluid checks as yesterday. Same tomorrow.

episodes.title: It Still Will Not Run
episodes.text: You put the tractor back together and turn the key. It sputters and dies, and something is clearly off in your rebuild.

choice.prompt: The rebuild will not hold. What do you do?

options.label: Shut it down and recheck your fit
options.outcome: You find a hose seated wrong and fix it. It starts rough, then settles into a steady idle.

options.label: Adjust the settings and test again
options.outcome: You make a small adjustment and try the controls. It runs, but you watch the gauges close for a repeat stall.

episodes.title: Writing Down Parts
episodes.text: You wash your hands and sit at the desk. You write down each repair you made and list every part you used. You close the work order when the list matches the bench.

episodes.title: Morning Growth Check
episodes.text: You walk the nursery rows with your notebook. You measure young plants and check soil moisture and air temperature. You write down growth and environmental numbers for the day.

episodes.title: Nursery Customers Arrive
episodes.text: You meet two retail customers by the display beds.

choice.prompt: Two customers want plants for display and you have limited staff to help. What do you do first?

options.label: Walk them to the ready sale beds yourself
options.outcome: You show them what is ready and they pick trays to buy. The potting work waits until you are back.

options.label: Ask a worker to show them while you finish watering
options.outcome: They get help right away and you stay on schedule. You check their order before they leave.

chat.text: We need plants for a front display. What is ready to go now?
Can you show us what holds up best for customers?

episodes.title: Eggs and Fry
episodes.text: You check the spawning tanks and the incubation trays. You look at water flow and watch the eggs and new fry. You note which tanks need cleaning or closer watching.

trial.title: Order the fish work
items: Watch eggs during incubation
Move fry to rearing tanks
Trap fish for spawning
Collect eggs for fertilizing
trial.explain: You trap fish first, then collect eggs, then watch incubation before rearing fry.

episodes.title: Same Numbers Again
episodes.text: You sit at the desk and copy production numbers into the record book. You enter the same growth and water readings you take every day. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Bugs in the Nursery
episodes.text: You find insects spreading on one bench of nursery plants. You check how far they have moved and what workers and spray you have today.

choice.prompt: The insects are spreading and you cannot cover everything at once. How do you use your resources?

options.label: Move workers to clear and treat that bench first
options.outcome: The crew stops potting and contains the insects on that bench. The rest of the nursery waits until tomorrow.

options.label: Split workers between treatment and normal watering
options.outcome: Watering stays done and treatment starts slower. You walk back later to see if the insects are still spreading.

options.label: Isolate the bench and call for advice before treating
options.outcome: The bench stays separate and you get clear steps for treatment. Work slows while you wait for an answer.

episodes.title: Moving Big Fish
episodes.text: You stand by the commercial tanks with nets and buckets ready. You help load mature fish and count them into the transport tank. You ride along to watch them released into the pond.

episodes.title: Opening the Nursery
episodes.text: You arrive at the nursery rows as the air is still cool. You walk past trays of young plants grown for sale. You check which benches need water first.

episodes.title: Morning Readings Again
episodes.text: You sit down with the same clipboard as yesterday. You copy growth numbers and water temperature into the log. You do the next row, then the next one, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Moving Market Fish
episodes.text: You stand by the holding tanks with your helper before the move.

choice.prompt: The pond is low and the tank fish are ready to move. Do you transfer them now?

options.label: Move them to the pond now
options.outcome: You net and carry the mature fish to the pond. Some stress in the shallow water and you watch them settle.

options.label: Hold them in the tank
options.outcome: You keep the mature fish in the commercial tank and top up aeration. You check the pond level again later.

chat.text: These ones ready for the pond?
Water looks low over there.

episodes.title: Checking Spawning Tanks
episodes.text: You bend over the brood tanks to check spawning. You look at the eggs set for incubation. You watch the fry rearing troughs swim in circles.

trial.title: Order the hatch work
items: Feed and watch the fry tanks
Trap ripe fish for spawning
Hold eggs through incubation
Strip and fertilize eggs from spawners
trial.explain: You trap fish first, then spawn, then incubate eggs, then rear fry.

episodes.title: Bugs in the House
episodes.text: You find insects spreading fast on the nursery plants. You have only so much spray and hands today. You must decide where it goes.

choice.prompt: Insects are spreading while water is short. How do you use what you have?

options.label: Treat the worst nursery block
options.outcome: You send help and spray to the worst block. The rest waits and you lose a few flats.

options.label: Split help across all blocks
options.outcome: You spread water and labor thin across blocks. The insects slow but stay in all houses.

options.label: Sacrifice one batch to save water
options.outcome: You pull and discard the worst batch. You save spray and water for the healthy plants.

episodes.title: Writing the Day
episodes.text: You sit down at the table with your notes. You record growth, production, and water readings for the day. You file the sheet for market records.

episodes.title: Morning Sketch Table
episodes.text: You arrive at your table and open your sketch pad. You draw rough shapes for a new jacket. You add a detailed view and write down the color and fabric.

episodes.title: Talking Through Ideas
episodes.text: You sit down with sales to talk through your sketches. They question one of your design ideas.

choice.prompt: Sales wants a cheaper idea for the jacket. What do you do?

options.label: Keep your design as drawn
options.outcome: You explain why the cut needs the current fabric. They agree to keep it for now.

options.label: Agree to simplify the design
options.outcome: You sketch the simpler version together. You note the new fabric and details.

chat.text: This jacket costs too much to make. Can we change it?
What if we keep the shape but use a simpler fabric?
Tell us what you think works.

episodes.title: Choosing Fabric Pieces
episodes.text: You lay out fabric swatches for the new pants. You feel the weight and stretch of each one. You pick the material and sewing method you will use.

trial.title: Pick the problem fabric
trial.scenario: You spread three material options for the pants on the table. Two match your notes for weight and stretch. One sags and will not hold the shape you sketched.
options: The wool that holds its shape
The thin fabric that sags at the knee
The cotton blend that matches your notes
trial.explain: The sagging fabric will not hold the shape you need.

episodes.title: Copying Spec Sheets
episodes.text: You sit and copy color names and material notes into each spec sheet. You check construction lines one by one. It is the same form as yesterday, and the same again tomorrow.

episodes.title: Sample Does Not Fit
episodes.text: You watch the model walk in the sample jacket. The shoulder pulls and the hem sits wrong. You need to change the design to fix it.

choice.prompt: The sample needs a fix before the next fitting. What do you change first?

options.label: Let out the shoulder seam
options.outcome: You mark the new seam line. The next sample hangs straighter.

options.label: Shorten the hem
options.outcome: You pin the new length in place. The model walks again so you can check it.

options.label: Change the fabric
options.outcome: You pull a sturdier swatch from stock. You attach it to the file for the maker.

episodes.title: Pricing The Styles
episodes.text: You sit with your list of finished styles. You add up material and making costs for each one. You write down the price for each style.

episodes.title: First House Call
episodes.text: You drive to the first house on your list. You carry in the reception box and set it by the TV. You connect the lines and get the picture up.

episodes.title: Pole Signal Check
episodes.text: You park under the utility pole and pull out your electronic test equipment. You clip on and measure the signal strength. You write down the reading and move to the next pole.

trial.title: Set up the box
items: You test the connected equipment to check it works
You set the equipment in place at the customer's home
You adjust the equipment for a clear picture
You connect the equipment to the line
trial.explain: You place it, connect it, adjust it, then test it.

episodes.title: Same Checks Again
episodes.text: You run the same line tests you ran yesterday. You check each reading and log it. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Showing The Remote
episodes.text: You sit with the subscriber after the install to explain the service.

choice.prompt: They still look unsure about the channels and owe the install fee. What do you do first?

options.label: Go through the channels again, then collect the fee
options.outcome: You show the buttons again until they can change channels. They pay the install fee and thank you.

options.label: Collect the fee and leave the manual
options.outcome: You take the install fee and leave the manual on the table. They nod but still stare at the remote.

chat.text: So which button is it for the channels?
You are still on site. Walk them through it.
And I pay you now for the install?

episodes.title: No Picture Call
episodes.text: You get sent back out because a street has no picture. You test the cables and find a fault in one section. The signal drops right at the break.

choice.prompt: You found the faulty section of cable. What do you do now?

options.label: Repair the faulty section now
options.outcome: You fix the section and test again until the signal holds. The picture comes back before you leave.

options.label: Mark it and call for a full line swap
options.outcome: You mark the bad section and record the readings for the crew. The house stays without picture until the swap.

options.label: Test the next section first
options.outcome: You test past the break to make sure there is only one fault. You confirm the one bad spot and then repair it.

episodes.title: Logging The Day
episodes.text: You sit in the van and record your test results for the day. You note the signal readings and where you found the fault. You close the log and head back.

episodes.title: The core work
episodes.text: You start the main work of a Film / Stage Lighting Technician — the core of the job, done properly, start to finish. No audience and no shortcut: this is the thing everything else in the day supports. This is the work the whole job is built around.

episodes.title: People time
episodes.text: People need things from you — questions, help, decisions. You deal with them one at a time, the way this job always does. Real people, real reactions — this is the human side of the job, as it actually feels.

choice.prompt: Someone you're working with asks you to take on one more thing — extra work, on top of everything already in front of you today.

options.label: Say yes and fit it in
options.outcome: You fit it in. The day runs longer, the work gets done properly — and the person who asked remembers that you said yes.

options.label: Say no, politely
options.outcome: You say no, and you say why. A short, slightly awkward moment — then the rest of your day stays yours.

options.label: Offer a smaller version
options.outcome: You offer the part you can actually do, and by when. Most days that's accepted — saying yes to everything is how this job burns people out.

episodes.title: Hands on
episodes.text: Hands-on time. You make, fix or adjust the real thing in front of you — the part of the job you can touch, and the part where skill is visible. Skilled, hands-on work — the part where being good at it shows.

trial.title: The check-in
trial.says: Hey — how's that thing coming along that you were working on?
options: It's on track. I'll flag it straight away if I need help or it slips.
Fine.
Honestly? Don't ask. It's a disaster.
trial.explain: The professional reply says where things stand and what happens next — short, honest, no drama.

episodes.title: The routine block
episodes.text: The same block as yesterday: the repeating tasks that never make the brochure. You do them again, carefully, because skipping them is exactly how mistakes happen. The same again tomorrow. This block repeats more than any other part of the job.

episodes.title: It goes wrong
episodes.text: Something goes wrong — it always does, some days. A problem lands on you that was in nobody's plan, and sorting it out is now your job. Unplanned and unavoidable — how the job feels when it pushes back.

episodes.title: The paperwork
episodes.text: End of day: notes, records, the write-up of everything you did. The work isn't finished until it's written down. Nobody's favourite part. It still has to be done, every day.

episodes.title: The core work
episodes.text: You start the main work of a Financial Analyst — the core of the job, done properly, start to finish. No audience and no shortcut: this is the thing everything else in the day supports. This is the work the whole job is built around.

episodes.text: Tools-and-systems time: you work the equipment and the screens of the trade until the thing in front of you does what it should. Skilled, hands-on work — the part where being good at it shows.

episodes.text: End of day: notes, records, the write-up of everything you did. The work isn't finished until it's written down. Nobody's favourite part. It still has to be done, every day.

episodes.title: Morning Gear On
episodes.text: You arrive at the station and pull on your fire-resistant clothing. You strap on your breathing apparatus and check the seal. It is the same check as yesterday, and the same as tomorrow.

episodes.title: Alarm Sounds Off
episodes.text: The alarm sounds for a fire call across town. You climb on the truck and ride out with the crew. You pull up to thin smoke showing from a low building.

choice.prompt: The crew is waiting to roll. Do you take the first seat out or stay back for the next call?

options.label: Ride out now
options.outcome: You go with the first crew and start work at the scene. The second crew covers the station until you return.

options.label: Stay for next call
options.outcome: You stay dressed and ready at the station. You take the next alarm for an automobile accident.

episodes.title: Moving Toward Heat
episodes.text: You are inside and moving toward the source of the fire. You keep the building layout in your head as you go. You watch the construction and materials to judge how the fire will act.

trial.title: Work toward the fire
items: Move toward the source of the fire
Recall the building materials in this part of the property
Picture the physical layout and construction design
Identify what type of fire you are facing
trial.explain: You read the building first, then name the fire, then move in.

episodes.title: Update On Radio
episodes.text: You step back to where you can see the fire clearly. You lift the two-way radio to report in.

chat.text: What are conditions on your side?
Copy that. Hold your position.
Report again if it spreads toward the rear.

episodes.title: Trapped Driver Inside
episodes.text: You respond to an automobile accident with the crew. A car is crushed at the edge of the road. You can hear someone calling from inside.

choice.prompt: Smoke is rising from the engine while the person is still trapped. What do you do first?

options.label: Start the rescue right away
options.outcome: You move in with the crew and begin pulling the survivor clear. The engine crew stands by to cool the smoke and heat.

options.label: Hold back and cool it first
options.outcome: You wait while water is put on the engine smoke. You move in to rescue once the crew gives the word.

options.label: Call for more help
options.outcome: You radio for another crew for the accident site. You stay with the trapped person until help arrives.

episodes.title: Person In Water
episodes.text: You answer a call for help at a water hazard near the road. You wade in with the crew in your protective gear. You support the survivor and bring them to dry ground.

episodes.title: Morning Assessment
episodes.text: You sit down with a new member before the gym gets busy. You ask about past injuries, daily movement, and what hurts or feels hard. You watch how they squat and reach to see what they can do.

choice.prompt: They tell you their back aches when they bend forward. How do you build their first plan?

options.label: Give them the standard full plan anyway
options.outcome: They try it but stop halfway because bending hurts. You have to cut movements out on the spot.

options.label: Leave out forward bending and start simpler
options.outcome: They finish the short plan without pain. You note to add more only when their back allows.

episodes.title: Planning the Routine
episodes.text: You sit with your notebook and plan today's class. You pick music with a steady beat and choose one movement for legs and one for shoulders. You keep the steps simple for stiff joints in the morning group.

episodes.title: Watching Form Closely
episodes.text: You stand at the side of the class and watch each person move. You notice backs rounding and knees caving in on the leg set. You walk over and show small fixes they can use right away.

trial.title: Spot the fix first
trial.scenario: Three people are moving at once. One holds their breath and rounds their back, one moves slowly but keeps a straight back, one stops to wipe sweat.
options: The person who stopped to wipe sweat
The person holding breath with rounded back
The person moving slowly with straight back
trial.explain: A rounded back held under effort needs the correction first to keep the movement safe.

episodes.title: Same Check-Ins Again
episodes.text: You go down the same list as yesterday. You check boxes for who came and how they did. You write the same short notes again for tomorrow.

episodes.title: Different Levels Together
episodes.text: You lead the afternoon class and the fitness levels are wide apart.

chat.text: I can't keep up with this move. My legs are done.
Show us what to do instead?
You show a slower march in place and they join back in.

episodes.title: When Knees Hurt
episodes.text: You check in with a regular and their progress has stalled. Their knees ache on the lunge pattern you gave them last week. You stop the set and look at how they move now.

choice.prompt: The rest of their plan is waiting. What do you do about the sore knees?

options.label: Push through the same lunges
options.outcome: They finish but walk out sore and limping. You have to change the plan tomorrow anyway.

options.label: Swap to a gentler move today
options.outcome: They finish the session with less pain. You write down the swap to track their progress.

options.label: End leg work and review upper body only
options.outcome: They leave feeling okay about today. You plan to rebuild the leg part before next time.

episodes.title: Checking Emergency Gear
episodes.text: You arrive early and step into the empty cabin. You open the overhead bins and under-seat stowage. You check the first aid kits, fire extinguishers, and oxygen bottles to see they are in working order.

episodes.title: Safety Demonstration
episodes.text: You stand at the front with the cabin crew. You announce the safety procedures over the speaker. You demonstrate the use of oxygen masks, seat belts, and life jackets.

trial.title: Spot what matters
trial.scenario: You finish demonstrating seat belts and oxygen masks. You look down the rows. You see one passenger already wearing a life jacket during boarding.
options: The life jacket worn now, before any instruction to use it
The seat belt you already demonstrated
The oxygen mask you already demonstrated
trial.explain: Life jackets are only handled when you demonstrate and instruct them.

episodes.title: Aisle Check Again
episodes.text: You walk the aisles before takeoff. You glance at seat belts, tray tables, and seats. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Watching Row Fourteen
episodes.text: You keep walking the cabin and watching faces and hands.

choice.prompt: He stands up again and steps into the aisle toward another passenger. What do you do?

options.label: Move close and watch him
options.outcome: You stand nearby where you can see his hands. He sits back down but keeps glaring down the row.

options.label: Speak to him calmly
options.outcome: You ask him to sit down and stay seated. He argues for a moment, then drops into his seat.

options.label: Call for crew help
options.outcome: You signal the senior crew member to come over. The two of you stand on either side of the row together.

chat.text: Row fourteen, aisle seat. He keeps standing and raising his voice.
He tried to push past me to the galley.
Keep eyes on him. Tell me if he moves again.

episodes.title: Before Landing Check
episodes.text: You walk the aisles again before landing. You check each row for seat belts and upright seats. You nod to passengers until the cabin is ready.

episodes.title: Leaving the Plane Fast
episodes.text: You hear the order to evacuate after the hard landing. You stand at your exit and shout the instructions. You direct passengers out and assist them down the slide.

choice.prompt: Smoke is near the front exit and passengers crowd toward you. What do you do?

options.label: Keep using your exit
options.outcome: You wave people toward your door. They move out quickly in a line to the grass.

options.label: Send them to the back exit
options.outcome: You point behind them and shout to go back. The line turns and moves toward the rear door.

episodes.title: Planning the Living Room
episodes.text: You arrive at the house and lay the floor sketch on the living room floor. You walk the room and watch where feet will move from door to couch to hall. You mark where the seams will sit for best looks and longest wear.

choice.prompt: The main walkway runs straight through the middle. Where do you put the seam?

options.label: Place the seam along the edge, out of the walkway
options.outcome: You shift the layout over. The seam sits near the wall where feet rarely land.

options.label: Place the seam across the middle of the walkway
options.outcome: You keep the layout centered. The seam takes direct foot traffic all day.

episodes.title: Checking the Subfloor
episodes.text: You kneel and run your hand across the bare floor. You find a raised ridge and a dip near the doorway. You note both spots that would show through or wear the carpet unevenly.

episodes.title: Rolling Out Carpet
episodes.text: You roll the carpet out across the room. You measure and mark it against the floor sketch. You cut it to size with the carpet knife and leave extra along the sides for final fitting.

trial.title: Cut Carpet to Size
items: Cut the carpet to size with the carpet knife
Roll out the carpet across the floor
Leave extra carpet for final fitting
Measure and mark following the floor sketch
trial.explain: You roll out first, then measure and mark, then cut, leaving extra for fitting.

episodes.title: Seaming Carpet Edges
episodes.text: You sit on the floor and join the next carpet edge. You press tape under the seam and run the heated iron slowly along it. You do the same seam again in the next room. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Dip Under the Seam
episodes.text: You press down near the doorway and the padding sinks into a soft dip. Your boss checks in about the holdup.

choice.prompt: The dip will show through the carpet at the seam. What do you do?

options.label: Stop and fix the dip before seaming
options.outcome: You fill and level the spot first. The seam lays flat and the carpet wears even.

options.label: Seam over the dip and keep going
options.outcome: You sew the edges and glue the tape. The carpet dips at the seam and wears uneven.

options.label: Cut around the dip and patch carpet later
options.outcome: You trim short to avoid it. You are left short on carpet for the wall fit.

chat.text: How does that spot look under the seam?
That dip will show through and wear fast. What do you want to do?

episodes.title: Trimming Along Walls
episodes.text: You kneel by the wall with the cut carpet in place. You cut and trim it tight along the baseboard and around the doorway projection. You finish the edge clean with the wall trimmer.

episodes.title: Morning Flower Order
episodes.text: You arrive and sit down with the wholesaler list. You order roses, greens, and tape for the week from the growers.

episodes.title: Picking Stems Together
episodes.text: You stand at the cooler pulling stems for today's orders. You hold lilies next to eucalyptus and swap in white stock until the mix feels right.

episodes.title: Planning The Design
episodes.text: You sit down with the card for a birthday arrangement. You think through color, stem length, and how the flowers hold, then pick a standard pattern to follow.

trial.title: Plan an arrangement
items: Select appropriate standard design pattern
Look over the client's requirements
Plan the arrangement for those requirements
Think about design and how materials behave
trial.explain: You start with what the client asked, then use what you know before you pick and plan.

episodes.title: Talking Price And Delivery
episodes.text: You meet a customer at the counter about anniversary flowers for Saturday.

choice.prompt: She wants pink, smaller, delivered Saturday at noon. How do you close it?

options.label: Confirm a price and arrangement type and write down Saturday noon delivery
options.outcome: You repeat back the type, price, and Saturday noon address and write it on the order. She pays the deposit.

options.label: Ask her to decide later and call back
options.outcome: You tell her to call back when she is sure. The Saturday slot stays open and you wait.

chat.text: We want something pink, not too big. What does that cost?
Can you bring it to the house around noon on Saturday?
So what date and place should I put down for us?

episodes.title: Van Runs Late
episodes.text: You load the afternoon deliveries and see one is due across town in twenty minutes. Traffic has put the driver behind and you have two boxes still waiting.

choice.prompt: The noon delivery is now going to be late. What do you do first?

options.label: Call the customer and give a new delivery time
options.outcome: You call and say you will be there by 3:15. You send the driver with that one first.

options.label: Send both deliveries out with no update
options.outcome: The driver leaves with both boxes on the old route. The customer waits without knowing.

options.label: Oversee a second drop to split the route
options.outcome: You ask the helper to take the second box while the driver takes the late one. Both leave at once.

episodes.title: Same Delivery Loop
episodes.text: You drive the same streets with arrangements in the back. You carry them to doors, get a signature, and drive on. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Morning Cooler Check
episodes.text: You arrive at the cold storage room. You open boxes and check the food products inside. You watch how workers handle and chill the food.

trial.title: Find the unsafe box
trial.scenario: You check three pallets of chicken. Two pallets are cold and sealed. One pallet sits warm with a broken seal and a sour smell.
options: The warm pallet with the broken seal
One of the cold sealed pallets
None of the pallets need attention
trial.explain: Warm temperature and a broken seal mean the food may not be safe to eat.

episodes.title: Walking the Produce Sheds
episodes.text: You walk the farm packing shed with the crew lead. You check crates and wash water against health and quality rules.

choice.prompt: One lot of greens looks wilted and dirty. It does not meet the health rule. What do you do now?

options.label: Hold the lot and explain why
options.outcome: You tag the lot to hold. The crew sets it aside and keeps packing the clean lots.

options.label: Let it pass to keep things moving
options.outcome: You let it go through. The unsafe lot moves forward and you must answer for it later.

chat.text: Morning. We kept the soft crates to the side like you asked.
Wash water was changed at eight. Want to check the log?

episodes.title: Same Plant Walk
episodes.text: You walk the slaughter floor again with your checklist. You look at the same drains, tables, and knives. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Labels and Seals
episodes.text: You stand by the graded cartons of fish. You stick on the grade labels and press the seals shut. You stack the sealed boxes for pickup.

episodes.title: Shutting the Line Down
episodes.text: You see meat on a dirty belt in the processing plant. The temperature log shows warm readings for an hour. You know the product is no longer safe.

choice.prompt: The line is still running and boxes are piling up. What do you do?

options.label: Stop the line and close the area
options.outcome: You order the line stopped and the area closed. The manager posts the notice and calls for cleanup.

options.label: Warn them and let it run
options.outcome: You give a warning and walk on. The unsafe meat keeps moving down the line.

options.label: Call your supervisor first
options.outcome: You step aside and call your supervisor. You wait by the line until you get a clear order.

episodes.title: Writing the Certificates
episodes.text: You sit down at the small office desk. You fill out the official grading certificates for today's sealed lots. You check each number before you sign.

episodes.title: Checking Morning Ingredients
episodes.text: You walk into the cool receiving room. You pick up tomatoes and press gently to check maturity. You set aside the soft ones that will not hold up in processing.

episodes.title: Same Sanitation Walk
episodes.text: You walk the same processing line with your checklist. You look at the floors, the surfaces, and the waste bins. You mark the same boxes you marked yesterday. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Testing Softer Texture
episodes.text: You sit down at the bench with two batches of sauce. You taste for flavor and check color and thickness. You note how a small recipe change shifts the texture.

trial.title: Sort the fruit delivery
items: Set aside fruit that is too soft for processing
Look at the new delivery of fruit
Send the firm fruit on to processing
Press and check each lot for maturity
trial.explain: You look first, then check maturity before you sort and send on what is stable.

episodes.title: Talking Through Sanitation
episodes.text: You stand by the wash station with a line worker. You both look at the standing water near the drain.

choice.prompt: The area is not staying clean and dry. What do you do now?

options.label: Show a different cleaning step now
options.outcome: You walk through the rinse and wipe again together. The area passes for now and you watch it again tomorrow.

options.label: Flag it for the sanitation fix list
options.outcome: You note the drain and water issue for repair. The line keeps running with extra wiping until it is fixed.

chat.text: It keeps pooling here after the rinse. Is this okay?
We wipe it down but it comes back by lunch.

episodes.title: Swollen Packs Found
episodes.text: You open the storage samples from last week. One pack is swollen and smells off. You pull the rest of the lot to check safety and quality.

choice.prompt: You have a suspect lot in storage. What do you do first?

options.label: Hold the lot and check more packs
options.outcome: You tag the lot on hold and open more packs to check. You keep the unsafe packs out of packing.

options.label: Taste a small bit to decide
options.outcome: You do not taste it and keep the packs sealed. You run safety checks instead of risking illness.

episodes.title: Writing Production Specs
episodes.text: You sit at your desk with today's notes. You write up the production specification and the waste and water steps. You file it so the next run follows the same standard.

episodes.title: The core work
episodes.text: You start the main work of a Food Stylist — the core of the job, done properly, start to finish. No audience and no shortcut: this is the thing everything else in the day supports. This is the work the whole job is built around.

episodes.title: People time
episodes.text: People need things from you — questions, help, decisions. You deal with them one at a time, the way this job always does. Real people, real reactions — this is the human side of the job, as it actually feels.

choice.prompt: Someone you're working with asks you to take on one more thing — extra work, on top of everything already in front of you today.

options.label: Say yes and fit it in
options.outcome: You fit it in. The day runs longer, the work gets done properly — and the person who asked remembers that you said yes.

options.label: Say no, politely
options.outcome: You say no, and you say why. A short, slightly awkward moment — then the rest of your day stays yours.

options.label: Offer a smaller version
options.outcome: You offer the part you can actually do, and by when. Most days that's accepted — saying yes to everything is how this job burns people out.

episodes.title: Hands on
episodes.text: Hands-on time. You make, fix or adjust the real thing in front of you — the part of the job you can touch, and the part where skill is visible. Skilled, hands-on work — the part where being good at it shows.

trial.title: The check-in
trial.says: Hey — how's that thing coming along that you were working on?
options: It's on track. I'll flag it straight away if I need help or it slips.
Fine.
Honestly? Don't ask. It's a disaster.
trial.explain: The professional reply says where things stand and what happens next — short, honest, no drama.

episodes.title: The routine block
episodes.text: The same block as yesterday: the repeating tasks that never make the brochure. You do them again, carefully, because skipping them is exactly how mistakes happen. The same again tomorrow. This block repeats more than any other part of the job.

episodes.title: It goes wrong
episodes.text: Something goes wrong — it always does, some days. A problem lands on you that was in nobody's plan, and sorting it out is now your job. Unplanned and unavoidable — how the job feels when it pushes back.

episodes.title: The paperwork
episodes.text: End of day: notes, records, the write-up of everything you did. The work isn't finished until it's written down. Nobody's favourite part. It still has to be done, every day.

episodes.title: Morning Menu Check
episodes.text: You arrive at the truck and open the master menu for today. You count staff, equipment, and supply needs against what you have. You write down what to bring in and what to hold back.

episodes.title: Daily Forms Fill
episodes.text: You sit down with the production, operational, and personnel forms. You enter the same numbers you enter every day. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Unhappy Customer Line
episodes.text: You step to the window to face a complaint about the food service. The line waits behind them.

choice.prompt: The customer wants an answer now at the window. How do you resolve it?

options.label: Remake the order now
options.outcome: You remake the order and hand them hot food. The line waits a little longer while you catch up.

options.label: Refund and apologize
options.outcome: You give the money back and say sorry for the wait. They leave without food and you note the complaint.

chat.text: This is not what I ordered and it is cold.
I waited a long time for this.
What are you going to do about it?

episodes.title: Special Diet Trays
episodes.text: You check a patient's nutritional needs and plan a special menu. You supervise the assembly of regular and special diet trays. You oversee the food trolley as it leaves for delivery to hospital patients.

trial.title: Put the tray job in order
items: Oversee the delivery of food trolleys to hospital patients
Plan special menus
Assess nutritional needs of patients
Supervise the assembly of regular and special diet trays
trial.explain: You assess first, then plan, then assemble, then deliver.

episodes.title: Second Complaint Escalates
episodes.text: A customer comes back angry about their food service. Their voice rises and other customers turn to look. You have to resolve the complaint before it spreads.

choice.prompt: They are shouting and will not step aside. What do you do?

options.label: Move them aside and listen
options.outcome: You step aside with them and hear the full complaint. You offer a fix and the line starts moving again.

options.label: Replace the meal on the spot
options.outcome: You make a fresh meal right away and hand it over. They calm down and walk away eating.

options.label: Close the window briefly
options.outcome: You pause service for a minute to handle it. The wait grows but the crowd settles.

episodes.title: Counting Cash Late
episodes.text: You close the window and pull out the cash receipts. You compile and balance the receipts for the day shift. You stack the cash and close the book.

episodes.title: The core work
episodes.text: You start the main work of a Franchise Owner (home services) — the core of the job, done properly, start to finish. No audience and no shortcut: this is the thing everything else in the day supports. This is the work the whole job is built around.

episodes.title: Night Call Pickup
episodes.text: You arrive at the small care home before sunrise. You speak quietly with the nurse on duty. You help move the person onto the stretcher and drive back carefully.

episodes.title: Sitting With Family
episodes.text: You sit down at the arrangement table with a daughter and son. You open your notebook to talk through casket selection and service plans.

choice.prompt: They look to you to help settle the obituary wording. What do you do?

options.label: Read back their two wordings and ask them to pick one line at a time
options.outcome: They pick one line at a time and you write down the final wording. You move on to the casket and service time.

options.label: Suggest you pick simple wording for now and revisit it later
options.outcome: They agree to pause and you note a draft. You set a time later today to confirm the final wording.

chat.text: We can't agree on the wording for the obituary notice.
And we aren't sure about the casket or the service time either.

episodes.title: Midday Care Check
episodes.text: You walk through the prep room and check each person in your care. You note the room log and straighten sheets the same way as yesterday. You lock the door and will do the same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Certificates And Permits
episodes.text: You sit down with the family information folder. You fill in names and dates for the death certificate and burial permit. You double-check spellings before you file them.

trial.title: Check the papers
trial.scenario: You are copying family details onto the death certificate and burial permit. The birth date looks different on two notes, and the permit still needs a signature.
options: File the forms as they are to keep things moving
Stop and confirm the right dates and get the needed details before filing
Skip the burial permit for now
trial.explain: The forms need correct information before they can be completed and filed.

episodes.title: Care Room Problem
episodes.text: You check on a person due for viewing tomorrow and see the preparation is not holding. The family is due to arrive soon. You step back and decide what to do first.

choice.prompt: The preparation needs more work before the family arrives. What do you do first?

options.label: Bring the family in now and explain while you keep working
options.outcome: The family waits in the room while you finish the care work. The viewing starts late and feels rushed.

options.label: Ask the family to wait and redo the preparation and care work
options.outcome: You close the room and complete the care work. You invite the family in when the person is ready.

options.label: Call a colleague to sit with the family while you work
options.outcome: Your colleague offers tea and explains the short wait. You finish the care work and open the room.

episodes.title: Quiet Embalming Work
episodes.text: You change and set out for the one case that needs embalming today. You work slowly and check your care as you go. You clean the room down when you finish.

episodes.title: Choosing the Finish
episodes.text: You sit with the customer beside a scratched oak table. You hold two stain cards up to the morning light.

choice.prompt: The customer looks to you to help pick the final color.

options.label: Suggest the medium stain
options.outcome: You rub a dab on the underside. They nod, and you write down medium walnut as the finish.

options.label: Ask them to take a day
options.outcome: They take the cards home. You cover the table and wait for their call tomorrow.

chat.text: I like the darker one, but will it hide the grain?
My mother had it lighter. I cannot decide.

episodes.title: Masking the Brass
episodes.text: You turn to a chair before any finish goes near it. You remove the handles and cover the cloth seat.

trial.title: Prep before finishing
items: Tape paper over areas that should stay clear
Lift off handles and knobs
Place the hardware in a tray to the side
Press the edges down and check for gaps
trial.explain: You clear the hardware first, then mask what must stay clean.

episodes.title: Filling the Crack
episodes.text: You find a long crack along a drawer side. You press wood putty into it and scrape it flush. You set it aside to harden.

episodes.title: Sanding Drawer Sides
episodes.text: You sit and sand drawer sides with sandpaper and steel wool. Same motion as yesterday. Same dust, same smooth check, same stack tomorrow.

episodes.title: Broken Chair Leg
episodes.text: You lift a chair and its leg wobbles loose in your hand. Glue and a screw could fix it, but the finish starts soon.

choice.prompt: The leg needs repair now or it will miss the finishing run.

options.label: Glue and screw it now
options.outcome: You glue the joint and drive the screw tight. You set the chair to dry while you keep working.

options.label: Set it aside for later
options.outcome: You tag the chair and move it off the bench. It waits for repair after the finishing is done.

episodes.title: Laying the Finish
episodes.text: You pick up a brush and lay stain into the wood grain. You rub it in by hand and seal it with lacquer. The surface turns warm and even.

episodes.title: New Character Morning
episodes.text: You sit down and open a blank biography doc. You write a short backstory for a new side character. You add one role-play choice that fits her past.

episodes.title: Same Numbers Again
episodes.text: You open the same balance sheet as yesterday. You nudge enemy health and reward numbers by a little. You save it and know you will do it again tomorrow.

episodes.title: Asking For Notes
episodes.text: You call the design and technical staff together online to hear their feedback.

choice.prompt: The team has given you conflicting feedback on the story and the mechanic. What do you integrate first?

options.label: Trim the slow storyline section
options.outcome: You cut two story beats and rewrite the bridge scene. The team agrees to test the shorter version next week.

options.label: Weaken the strong role-play move
options.outcome: You lower the move's effect and update the description. The next playtest shows players use other options more.

chat.text: That second storyline drags. Players will get stuck there.
And the new role-play move feels too strong.
What do you want to change first?

episodes.title: Building Small Puzzle
episodes.text: You sit with a new mission idea. You sketch a locked door with three clues. You tune it so the solution feels fair.

trial.title: Order the mission build
items: You place the clues and locks in the level
You write down the goal of the mission
You play through it to check it feels fair
You set the rules for how it can be solved
trial.explain: You set the goal first, then the rules, then the placement, then you test it.

episodes.title: Playtest Breaks Down
episodes.text: You watch a fresh playtest fall apart. Players fail the same challenge five times and quit. The balance feels off and the launch build is close.

choice.prompt: The challenge is too hard and players are quitting. How do you adjust the balance now?

options.label: Lower the challenge difficulty now
options.outcome: You reduce enemy damage and add one extra hint. Players finish the level but the win feels a little easy.

options.label: Keep it hard and watch one more test
options.outcome: You leave the numbers alone and run another test. Players quit in the same spot again and you lose the day.

options.label: Split the challenge into two steps
options.outcome: You break the fight into two smaller parts with a break between. Most testers get through after two tries.

episodes.title: Review Notes Filed
episodes.text: You sit down to close the regular design review. You write what was decided about story, missions, and balance. You send the notes to the design and technical staff.

episodes.title: Carrying Springs Up
episodes.text: You arrive at the first house and set your ladder at the door. You lift a spring and climb steady to the top. You get set to attach it to the track.

trial.title: Install the spring set
items: Attach springs to tracks to install the system
Carry the spring to the top of the door
Set the ladder at the door
Climb the ladder with the spring
trial.explain: You set the ladder first, then carry and climb before you attach anything.

episodes.title: Winding the Spring
episodes.text: You stand close and grip your winding arm. You push upward in slow turns to wind the large spring. You pause and check the tension before you let go.

episodes.title: Heavy Door Check
episodes.text: You meet the owner in the garage by the opener.

choice.prompt: The door is too heavy and the opener strains. What do you adjust first?

options.label: Adjust the door and opener for correct effort
options.outcome: You adjust the door and tweak the opener. The door lifts with normal effort again.

options.label: Leave it heavy and tell them to pull harder
options.outcome: They keep struggling with the heavy door. You get called back the same week.

chat.text: It takes both hands to lift it now.
Check the effort and the opener setting.
Can you make it feel normal again?

episodes.title: Same Bolts Again
episodes.text: You sit down with your hand tools for worn door parts. You repair and replace the same kind of worn pieces. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Broken Part Call
episodes.text: You get to the next door and find a broken part hanging loose. The door will not move right and the owner waits. You hold your hand tools and decide how to start.

choice.prompt: The door has a worn broken part. What do you do now?

options.label: Repair the part now with hand tools
options.outcome: You fix it with your hand tools. The door moves and you finish on time.

options.label: Replace the broken part with a new one
options.outcome: You swap the broken part out. The door runs clean and you pack up.

options.label: Leave it and come back later
options.outcome: The door stays stuck. You have to drive back tomorrow to do it.

episodes.title: Ordering New Springs
episodes.text: You sit in the truck and list what ran out today. You order replacement springs and sections for tomorrow. You close the book and head back.

episodes.title: Morning Schedule Check
episodes.text: You arrive at the site trailer before the crews. You sit down with the day's work plan on the table. You line up deliveries and crew start times to meet the deadline.

episodes.title: Crew Start Up
episodes.text: You gather the crew by the foundation for the morning assignments.

choice.prompt: The truck is late and the crew is waiting. What do you do first?

options.label: Shift the crew to east side work
options.outcome: They start framing and stay busy. You update the schedule to fit the late delivery in later.

options.label: Keep everyone waiting by the pour site
options.outcome: The crew stands around for an hour. You lose framing time you could have used.

chat.text: Boss, the concrete truck is running late again.
Understood. I will check on it now.
Should we start framing on the east side while we wait?

episodes.title: Same Quality Walk
episodes.text: You walk the same quality checklist you walked yesterday. You check the same joints, surfaces, and fasteners. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Numbers and Progress
episodes.text: You sit back down in the trailer with receipts and time sheets. You update the cost tracking sheet and write the progress report. You prepare the budget estimate to send out.

episodes.title: Failed Safety Rail
episodes.text: You inspect the second floor edge during your walk. You see a guardrail section is loose and leaning. Work is still moving near the open edge.

choice.prompt: Workers are close to the loose rail. What do you do?

options.label: Stop work in the area and fix the rail
options.outcome: Everyone steps back while two workers secure the rail. Work near the edge restarts once it holds firm.

options.label: Flag it and keep work moving
options.outcome: Work continues next to the loose rail. Someone could fall before it gets fixed.

options.label: Rope off the edge and call maintenance
options.outcome: The area stays closed until the rail is repaired. The rest of the site keeps working.

episodes.title: Final Code Walk
episodes.text: You do one last walk to check building and safety code compliance. You look over rails, stairs, and electrical covers. You note what still needs fixing before tomorrow.

trial.title: What Needs Attention First
trial.scenario: You review the second floor for code compliance. One stair handrail is loose, one outlet cover is cracked, and one guardrail section is missing entirely.
options: The missing guardrail section at the open edge
The cracked outlet cover in the hallway
The loose handrail that still stands
trial.explain: The missing guardrail leaves an open fall edge and must be fixed first.

episodes.title: The core work
episodes.text: You start the main work of a General Surgeon — the core of the job, done properly, start to finish. No audience and no shortcut: this is the thing everything else in the day supports. This is the work the whole job is built around.

episodes.title: People time
episodes.text: People need things from you — questions, help, decisions. You deal with them one at a time, the way this job always does. Real people, real reactions — this is the human side of the job, as it actually feels.

choice.prompt: Someone you're working with asks you to take on one more thing — extra work, on top of everything already in front of you today.

options.label: Say yes and fit it in
options.outcome: You fit it in. The day runs longer, the work gets done properly — and the person who asked remembers that you said yes.

options.label: Say no, politely
options.outcome: You say no, and you say why. A short, slightly awkward moment — then the rest of your day stays yours.

options.label: Offer a smaller version
options.outcome: You offer the part you can actually do, and by when. Most days that's accepted — saying yes to everything is how this job burns people out.

episodes.title: Hands on
episodes.text: Hands-on time. You make, fix or adjust the real thing in front of you — the part of the job you can touch, and the part where skill is visible. Skilled, hands-on work — the part where being good at it shows.

trial.title: The check-in
trial.says: Hey — how's that thing coming along that you were working on?
options: It's on track. I'll flag it straight away if I need help or it slips.
Fine.
Honestly? Don't ask. It's a disaster.
trial.explain: The professional reply says where things stand and what happens next — short, honest, no drama.

episodes.title: The routine block
episodes.text: The same block as yesterday: the repeating tasks that never make the brochure. You do them again, carefully, because skipping them is exactly how mistakes happen. The same again tomorrow. This block repeats more than any other part of the job.

episodes.title: It goes wrong
episodes.text: Something goes wrong — it always does, some days. A problem lands on you that was in nobody's plan, and sorting it out is now your job. Unplanned and unavoidable — how the job feels when it pushes back.

episodes.title: The paperwork
episodes.text: End of day: notes, records, the write-up of everything you did. The work isn't finished until it's written down. Nobody's favourite part. It still has to be done, every day.

episodes.title: Morning Chart Review
episodes.text: You arrive early and open your case list. You look through intake forms and family histories. You mark two families who may be at risk for an inherited condition.

episodes.title: Talking Through Testing
episodes.text: You sit down with a couple to talk about testing options.

choice.prompt: They ask what to do next. How do you guide them?

options.label: Walk through risks and limits
options.outcome: You explain the risks, benefits, and limitations of each option. They take the handout home to think it over.

options.label: Give them more time
options.outcome: You pause the discussion and offer to meet again next week. They thank you and leave without deciding today.

chat.text: We are not sure if we want the test at all.
What would it actually tell us?
And what would it not tell us?

episodes.title: Reading New Results
episodes.text: You open a new lab report at your desk. You compare the finding to the patient's history. You call the referring physician to share what you found.

trial.title: Sort the result steps
items: You explain what the result means in plain language
You open the lab report and read the finding
You document who you told and what you said
You check the family history against the result
trial.explain: You read first, check context, explain it, then document it.

episodes.title: Same Pedigrees Again
episodes.text: You sit back down with the stack of family histories. You go through each one the same way as yesterday. Same boxes, same notes, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Unexpected Lab Result
episodes.text: You get a positive result you did not expect. You bring the patient and her sister into the quiet room. You explain what the finding means for both of them.

choice.prompt: She starts crying and says she cannot hear more. What do you do?

options.label: Pause and offer reassurance
options.outcome: You stop, sit with her, and give her time to breathe. You go over the next steps slowly when she is ready.

options.label: Continue with key facts
options.outcome: You gently cover the most important information she needs today. You arrange a follow-up call to go over the rest.

options.label: Invite the sister in closer
options.outcome: You ask if she wants her sister to stay and listen with her. You repeat the main points so they both hear them together.

episodes.title: Writing Up Notes
episodes.text: You sit at your desk and open your report template. You write a detailed consultation note on today's cases for the referring physician.

episodes.title: Gathering Morning Files
episodes.text: You sit down at your desk and open the project folder. You pull together aerial photographs, survey notes, and old records. You stack reports and original maps beside them for the day's work.

episodes.title: Tracing Aerial Detail
episodes.text: You lean into the precision stereoplotting viewer. You trace control points, streams, and hills from the aerial photo. You add roads and buildings with careful drafting moves.

episodes.title: Checking Legal Boundaries
episodes.text: You open legal records to check a property line. Two old descriptions do not quite match. You compare the wording against the survey notes on your screen.

choice.prompt: The records disagree on one boundary corner. What do you do next?

options.label: Hold the line and flag it
options.outcome: You leave the boundary as drawn and note the conflict for review. The map waits until the record is clarified.

options.label: Use the newer record
options.outcome: You draw the boundary from the newer record and note the source. The older description stays in the file for reference.

episodes.title: Same Checks Again
episodes.text: You open the next composition in the queue. You run the same completeness check you did yesterday. You mark it and move to the next one, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Fixing the Terrain Model
episodes.text: You open the three-dimensional terrain model on your screen. You adjust a trace map and clean up a table. You redraw a small chart to match the new detail.

trial.title: Put map prep in order
items: Pull the original maps for reference
Collect aerial photographs for the area
Gather survey notes and records
Pull reports for background
trial.explain: You start with photos and notes before reports and original maps.

episodes.title: Missing Line on Map
episodes.text: You inspect the final composition and spot a missing contour. Your deadline is close.

choice.prompt: You see a gap in the final map. What do you do?

options.label: Stop it and fix the gap
options.outcome: You hold the map back and add the missing detail. You run the completeness check again before release.

options.label: Send it and note the gap
options.outcome: You send the composition with a note about the missing detail. You log it to correct in the next revision.

chat.text: Did you see the final check? Something looks off.
Can you confirm if the composition is complete before we send it?

episodes.title: Reading the Morning Plans
episodes.text: You arrive and unroll the blueprints on the table. You trace the window marks to find size, shape, and thickness of each pane. You note where the framing goes and what the install steps call for.

episodes.title: Checking the Plumb Line
episodes.text: You hold your plumb line against the wall and watch it settle. You set your level on the ceiling track and read the bubble. You mark a low spot that will throw the frame off.

trial.title: What Needs Fixing First
trial.scenario: You check a doorway opening before setting the frame. The plumb line hangs free on the left but touches the wall on the right. The level shows the header tilts down on one end.
options: The side wall is out of plumb and will pinch the frame
The glass color is wrong for the room
The suction cups need more air pressure
trial.explain: A wall that is not straight will keep the frame from sitting square.

episodes.title: Setting Another Frame
episodes.text: You lift another pre-assembled wood frame into place and drive it in with your hand tools. You shim it, check it, and move to the next one. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Fitting the Metal Sash
episodes.text: You are fitting aluminum sashes with your coworker when the molding will not sit flat.

choice.prompt: The molding will not sit flat. What do you do?

options.label: Trim and refit the molding
options.outcome: You take it down, trim the edge, and reset it. It sits flat and you move on.

options.label: Force it in and move on
options.outcome: You push it tight and screw it down. It holds for now but the corner stays lifted.

chat.text: This corner keeps riding up. You seeing that too?
Check the cut before you force it. We only have one spare.

episodes.title: Glass in the Air
episodes.text: You guide the hoist as the big pane rises off the rack. You see one edge slip a finger-width as a suction cup loses grip. You hold the tag line and call for the lift to stop.

choice.prompt: The pane is hanging uneven on the suction cups. What do you do?

options.label: Lower it back to the rack
options.outcome: You lower the glass back down to rest. You reattach the suction cups and start the lift again.

options.label: Reach up to steady the low edge
options.outcome: You step in and push up on the low edge. The pane steadies but your hands take the weight.

episodes.title: Locking the Last Molding
episodes.text: You set the steel molding over the afternoon pane and press it into the frame. You tighten it down and run your finger along the edge to feel for gaps. You wipe the glass and step back to check the line.

episodes.title: Morning Donor Search
episodes.text: You sit down at your desk and open your laptop. You look through a list of small businesses that gave last year. You pick two new names to learn more about and follow up with.

episodes.title: Asking for Support
episodes.text: You open an email draft to a local business owner. You explain what the program needs this spring. You pause before you ask for a cash donation.

choice.prompt: You are ready to make the ask. How do you ask for the donation?

options.label: Ask for a specific small cash gift
options.outcome: You ask for $250 to cover supplies. The owner says she will think about it and replies by Friday.

options.label: Ask for an in-kind donation instead
options.outcome: You ask if they can donate printed flyers. The owner says yes and asks you to send the details.

episodes.title: Updating Contact Lists
episodes.text: You open the donor database. You fix spelling in names and add new phone numbers. It is the same list as yesterday and will be the same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Writing Thank You Notes
episodes.text: You pull up yesterday's gifts on your screen. You write a short thank-you letter to each donor. You sign your name and press send.

trial.title: Put the thank-you in order
items: Send the letter to the donor
Write a short note mentioning their gift
Check the donor's name and gift amount
Sign the finished letter
trial.explain: You check the details first so the note is correct before you send it.

episodes.title: Donor Hesitates to Commit
episodes.text: You are on a call with a donor who said yes last week. Now he sounds unsure about giving.

choice.prompt: He has not said no, but he has not said yes. What do you do?

options.label: Offer a smaller commitment
options.outcome: You ask if a smaller gift this month would work. He agrees to $100 and asks you to email the form.

options.label: Offer to pause and call later
options.outcome: You say you can check back next month. He thanks you and says to call after the first.

options.label: Thank him and let it go
options.outcome: You thank him for his time and end the call. You mark him as declined for now in your notes.

chat.text: I'm not sure we can do this right now.
Things are tight this month.

episodes.title: Logging Today's Changes
episodes.text: You sit back down and open the donor database again. You add today's replies and update who gave and who declined. You save and close the file for the day.
